headline: Two friends killed after train hits motorcycle in Chuadanga
summary: The victims, aged 17 and 22, died on the spot when the Mahananda Mail train struck their bike at a rail crossing in Damurhuda.
details: Two friends were killed and another injured after their motorcycle was hit by a train while crossing a rail line in the Damurhuda upazila of Chuadanga.
The incident occurred around 5:30 PM on Thursday in the Dudhpatila area of the upazila headquarters union.
The deceased have been identified as 17-year-old Raihan Raj from Saradbariya village and 22-year-old Abdullah Al Mamun from Mortuzapur village.
A third friend, 22-year-old Abdul Kader, sustained severe leg injuries and was rushed to Chuadanga Sadar Hospital before being transferred to Dhaka for further treatment.
According to witnesses, the three friends were out for a ride when the Mahananda Mail train, coming from Khulna, struck their motorcycle at the Dudhpatila rail crossing.
Railway police and local police arrived at the scene to complete legal formalities, and the bodies were recovered by the GRP by 8:45 PM.
The bodies were handed over to the families at 11:00 PM without autopsies following written requests from the bereaved families.
Damurhuda Model Police Station and Railway Police coordinated the recovery and identification process.
caption:
A ride with friends turned tragic when a train struck their motorcycle in Chuadanga, leaving two dead and one critically injured.

Two friends were killed and another injured after their motorcycle was hit by a train while crossing a rail line in the Damurhuda upazila of Chuadanga.

The incident occurred around 5:30 PM on Thursday in the Dudhpatila area of the upazila headquarters union.

The deceased have been identified as 17-year-old Raihan Raj from Saradbariya village and 22-year-old Abdullah Al Mamun from Mortuzapur village.

A third friend, 22-year-old Abdul Kader, sustained severe leg injuries and was rushed to Chuadanga Sadar Hospital before being transferred to Dhaka for further treatment.

According to witnesses, the three friends were out for a ride when the Mahananda Mail train, coming from Khulna, struck their motorcycle at the Dudhpatila rail crossing.

Railway police and local police arrived at the scene to complete legal formalities, and the bodies were recovered by the GRP by 8:45 PM.

The bodies were handed over to the families at 11:00 PM without autopsies following written requests from the bereaved families.

Damurhuda Model Police Station and Railway Police coordinated the recovery and identification process.

headline_marked: UK proposes [[technical education support and expanded investment]] in Bangladesh
headline: UK proposes technical education support and expanded investment in Bangladesh
summary: British High Commissioner Sarah Cook met with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman to discuss deepening trade ties and aviation sector investments.
details: British High Commissioner Sarah Cook met with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the parliament complex on Thursday to discuss bilateral cooperation.
The UK has proposed providing support for technical education and training in Bangladesh to enhance the country's workforce skills.
Both leaders discussed expanding bilateral trade and increasing British investment, which is expected to create new employment opportunities for Bangladeshis.
High Commissioner Cook expressed specific interest in British investment within the aviation sector, following the opening of the third terminal of Shahjalal International Airport.
The meeting was attended by Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman and the Prime Minister's Foreign Affairs Advisor Humaiun Kobir.
caption:
The UK is looking to boost investment and technical education in Bangladesh. New opportunities in aviation and trade are on the table.

British High Commissioner Sarah Cook met with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman at the parliament complex on Thursday to discuss bilateral cooperation.

The UK has proposed providing support for technical education and training in Bangladesh to enhance the country's workforce skills.

Both leaders discussed expanding bilateral trade and increasing British investment, which is expected to create new employment opportunities for Bangladeshis.

High Commissioner Cook expressed specific interest in British investment within the aviation sector, following the opening of the third terminal of Shahjalal International Airport.

The meeting was attended by Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman and the Prime Minister's Foreign Affairs Advisor Humaiun Kobir.

#Bangladesh #UK #Trade #Investment #Education #Diplomacy
